title: Compatibility facade for vector iterator: error semantics, pagination, and backoff playbook
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Problem: multiple client ecosystems depend on legacy embeddings + rerank endpoints that expose divergent pagination semantics and inconsistent HTTP errors. This causes duplicate items, lost continuation cursors, and confusion around retries and backoff. Goal: deliver a compatibility facade (server-side shim and SDK helpers) that normalizes pagination cursors, unifies HTTP error semantics, and exposes explicit negotiation headers so both legacy and modern clients can coexist without behavioral regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Legacy iterator clients can page through large result sets without duplicates or gaps using existing client code (no protocol changes).

2) HTTP error surface is normalized: transient server capacity errors map to 503/Retry-After or 429/Retry-After, client input errors map to 400/422, and idempotency/body-mismatch errors map to 409 with clear retry guidance.
3) New header-based feature negotiation (X-Embed-Iterator-Contract) allows opt-in to strict cursor semantics for modern SDKs.
4) SDK shim provided for JS/python that converts streaming/line-delimited rerank responses into cursored pages and exposes resume tokens for robust resume/retry semantics.
5) Observability: metrics for resumed streams, cursor-expires, normalized-error-rate, and client-negotiation-adoption are emitted to console dashboards.
6) End-to-end test suite (unit + integration) covering network errors, partial stream interruption, duplicate item prevention, and backoff behaviors with deterministic outcomes.
decisions: Adopt header-based capability negotiation instead of URL-versioning to avoid proliferating endpoints.
Define three canonical cursor types: ephemeral-offset, resume-token (opaque), and stable-checkpoint. Clients will be advised which is active via response headers.
Map internal streaming chunk errors to canonical HTTP codes using a centralized translator middleware so downstream proxies see consistent signals.
Expose X-Retry-After-Ms (milliseconds) plus standard Retry-After to support sub-second guidance for high-throughput clients.

Fallback behavior: when capacity-constrained, return a 200 with an abbreviated page + X-Degraded: capacity hint and clear Link header for next. This preserves availability while signaling quality degradation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: server-side translator middleware behind feature flag for 10% of traffic to detect regressions (2 weeks). Phase 2: SDK shim beta (JS + Python) and docs for opt-in negotiation (4 weeks). Phase 3: full rollout with monitoring + automatic fallback policies and a two-week rollback window. Communications: changelog, migration guide, and in-console banner for users relying on legacy endpoints.
test_matrix: Scenario: full streaming interruption mid-page -> Expectation: resume-token returned, SDK retries with idempotency token and completes without duplicates.
Scenario: transient capacity spike -> Expectation: 503 + Retry-After header; SDK backs off exponential jitter and resumes at resume-token.
Scenario: legacy client with offset cursor -> Expectation: server treats offset as ephemeral-offset and returns consistent next-offset link header; no duplication.
Scenario: malformed client payload -> Expectation: 400 with error code and pointer to invalid field; no retry hint provided.
Scenario: quota-exceeded -> Expectation: 429 with X-Quota-Reset and suggestion to contact support for Dedicated capacity upgrade.
implementation_notes: Middleware will live in router layer (runtime) to map internal stream error events to HTTP semantics and add feature negotiation headers.
Introduce new telemetry tags: iterator_contract_v, resume_token_issued, resume_attempts, normalized_error_class.
SDK shim design: non-breaking wrappers that detect streaming or cursor endpoints and translate both ways; provide an escape hatch to return raw streaming frames.
Ensure Link header follows RFC 8288 semantics for next rel with token param (e.g., <https://api.run/redwood/embed?page=1&cursor=abc>; rel="next").
Coordinate with Console team to display per-route normalized-error-rate and customer-visible guidance when degradations occur.
migration_steps: 1) Deploy translator middleware behind feature flag; run synthetic traffic against legacy clients to validate behavior.
2) Publish SDK shim v0.1 beta and sample migration guide showing 3 lines of code change for JS/python.
3) Enable header negotiation for a subset of modern SDKs to test strict cursor semantics.
4) Iterate on error-mapping rules based on Canary metrics; expand rollout to 50% then 100%.
5) Remove temporary debug headers after 90 days once adoption and stability validated.
monitoring_playbook: Alert: normalized-error-rate > 2% for > 5 minutes -> page on-call SRE + PM.
Alert: resume-token-issuance spike -> investigate upstream model/reranker streaming timeouts.
Dashboard: per-client contract-version adoption, duplicate-item-rate, average-resume-latency, retry-success-rate.
Runbook: manual patch to toggle feature-flag and return to previous behavior within 5 minutes.
